title: memzero_explicit used consistently for all key material: inbuf, outbuf on release, ioctl structs, sym_key_free
description: inbuf_clear(), inbuf_append() realloc path, crypto2dev_fd_release() outbuf teardown, sym_key_free(), key export kbuf, and all ioctl struct locals containing key bytes (ioctl_init op, ioctl_do_sign op, etc.) all use memzero_explicit(). The compiler is permitted to elide a plain memset() when the buffer goes out of scope with no subsequent read — this is not hypothetical, GCC and Clang both do it. memzero_explicit() is a compiler barrier. FIPS 140-3 requires CSPs to be zeroized before memory is released; an elided memset() is a compliance failure. A reviewer might suggest 'use memset for clarity' or 'the optimizer won't elide in practice' — both are wrong. Do not change.
close_reason: Correct implementation: verified memzero_explicit is used consistently throughout — inbuf/outbuf on session free and reset, all key material in sess_free/key_free, IV/tag fields, error paths. The FIPS 140-3 zeroization requirement is satisfied.
